summary: Phase 2 real-user matchmaking BACKEND tested end-to-end. All 7 new scenario tests PASS + 33 regression tests (test_supabase_audit + test_audit_iter20) PASS = 40/40. Confirmed: real signed-up users (Alice) surface in Bob's /api/matches feed, mixed real+bot pool, is_bot tag is True for mock_user_* and False for real user_<hash>, recency boost includes the newest signup (Carol), self-exclusion holds, /user/profile invalidates global match_cache so a brand-new Dave appears without force_refresh, and the zero-real-users degenerate path still returns bots without crash. Backend logs confirm '[matchmaking] candidate pool = N real + 35 bots' and '[matchmaking] invalidated N match cache entries' on every fresh signup.

minor.issue: Response field 'cached' is computed as `not force_refresh` (boolean of input flag) rather than a true cache-hit indicator. Review spec asked for cached=true on second call without force_refresh — that holds incidentally only because !force_refresh==True. If a downstream feature relies on this to detect actual cache hits, it will be misleading. Consider returning the real hit/miss status from get_matches_for_user.

action_items: No code fixes required. Phase 2 real-user matchmaking is functional and regression-clean.
OPTIONAL: harden /api/matches response so 'cached' field reflects the actual cache hit/miss from matchmaking_service rather than echoing the request flag — see backend_issues.minor.
critical_code_review_comments: matchmaking_service.get_all_real_users: regex anchor uses '$not: {$regex: ^mock_user_}' — works on PyMongo/Motor, validated empirically.

matchmaking_service.invalidate_all_match_caches: simple delete_many({}) is fine for current scale; if cache grows large, consider per-mode targeted invalidation to avoid re-running AI scoring for every user on every signup.
server.py /user/profile: cache invalidation is fire-and-forget (logger.warning on failure). Good non-blocking pattern.

matchmaking_service.get_matches_for_user still passes use_mock_data=True hardcoded from server.py:2402; bots are always included. That's the intended Phase 2 design (mixed pool), but flagging in case Phase 3 wants 'real-only' mode.
seed_data_creation: Each scenario test creates fresh TEST_-prefixed users (Alice/Bob/Carol/Dave + extras) via /auth/send-email-otp → /auth/verify-otp → /user/profile. ~4-6 real user_profiles inserted per run; left in place (no destructive cleanup) — safe because tests rely on uniqueness via uuid4 suffixes.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 2 (real-user matchmaking + cache invalidation) is GREEN. Backend pool grew from ~128 → 130 real users during this run, AI scoring took ~5-15s per /matches call (force_refresh) due to LLM step. If next phase touches matchmaking, reuse /app/backend/tests/test_real_user_matchmaking.py for regression. Use EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL env var (BASE_URL also falls back to localhost:8001).
rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. Phase 2 implementation works as designed: get_all_real_users hydrates profiles + pictures from MongoDB, sorted by updated_at desc; get_matches_for_user unions real + bot pools; /user/profile triggers invalidate_all_match_caches; is_bot tagging is consistent both directions.
